what_it_is: Server-to-server method (Meta Conversions API, and equivalents at Google, TikTok, Snap) for sending conversion event data directly from an advertiser's server to ad platforms, bypassing browser-based pixels and cookies.
why_marketers_care: As of 2026 CAPI is treated as table stakes, not an advanced optimization, because it restores signal lost to iOS privacy changes, ad blockers, and cookie restrictions, improving match rates and automated bidding accuracy.
example: Meta Conversions API paired with the Meta Pixel for deduplicated, more accurate event matching, as widely documented in 2026 implementation guides.
first_seen_or_mainstream: Meta CAPI launched 2020-2021 but became a baseline, non-optional requirement for advertisers through 2025-2026 as third-party signal loss deepened.
notes: Not newly coined, but its status shifted from optional to mandatory baseline within the Sept 2024-Sept 2026 window, which is why marketers now treat it as a must-know acronym.

what_it_is: Apple's successor to SKAdNetwork (SKAN), introduced at WWDC 2024 and substantially upgraded at WWDC 2025 (rolled out with iOS 18.4), for privacy-preserving mobile ad attribution.
why_marketers_care: Adds configurable attribution windows, native re-engagement attribution, and developer testing mode that SKAN lacked, directly changing how mobile UA marketers measure iOS campaigns; both frameworks run side by side in 2026.
example: Apple Search Ads added support for both SKAdNetwork and AdAttributionKit, per Singular's 2026 coverage.
first_seen_or_mainstream: Announced WWDC 2024, expanded WWDC 2025, real-world marketer discussion peaked through 2025-2026.
notes: Note per Kochava (2026): actual adoption of AAK is still negligible versus legacy SKAN as of mid-2026, despite heavy trade-press coverage.

expansion: Global Privacy Platform (renamed Global Privacy Protocol in early 2025)
term: GPP (Global Privacy Platform / Global Privacy Protocol)
what_it_is: IAB Tech Lab technical standard for transmitting consent, opt-out, and other privacy signals from sites/apps to ad tech vendors across multiple regulatory regimes (GDPR, US state laws, etc.) in one standardized string.
why_marketers_care: The IAB Tech Lab renamed it to Global Privacy Protocol in 2025 to clarify it's a standard, not a product; it now covers new US state sections (Maryland, Indiana, Kentucky, Rhode Island) and Google began supporting GPP National v2 from September 2025, making it operationally required for compliant programmatic buying.
example: Google Ad Manager's support for the IAB's Global Privacy Platform, documented by Google in its Ad Manager Help Center.
first_seen_or_mainstream: Standard developed 2022-2023, renamed and expanded through 2025 with new state sections effective Oct 2025-Jan 2026.

what_it_is: IAB Europe's updated consent-signaling standard, released 19 June 2025, which makes the 'Disclosed Vendors' section of the TC string mandatory to give technical proof (not just policy) that vendors were actually disclosed to users.
why_marketers_care: Migration deadline is 28 February 2026; after that date TC strings built on TCF 2.2 become technically invalid, and non-compliant ad requests default to Google's 'Limited Ads' mode, which can cut programmatic revenue by 40-60%.
example: Google Ads announced TCF 2.3 compliance becomes mandatory 28 Feb 2026 for all advertisers serving ads in Europe, per Dataslayer's 2026 briefing.
first_seen_or_mainstream: Released June 2025; enforcement and marketer urgency peak Sept 2025-Feb 2026.
notes: TCF itself is an older framework (since 2018); it is included here specifically because version 2.3 is the newly mainstream, deadline-driven update marketers must act on in this window.

what_it_is: A browser-level opt-out signal that automatically tells websites not to sell or share a visitor's personal information for targeted advertising, functioning as a universal opt-out mechanism.
why_marketers_care: 12 US states require GPC compliance by 1 January 2026 (California, Colorado, Connecticut, Montana, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, Minnesota, Maryland, Delaware, Oregon, Texas); California's CPPA voted in August 2026 to formally name GPC inside CCPA regulations, and joint AG enforcement sweeps began September 2025.
example: Connecticut, California, and Colorado Attorneys General jointly sent enforcement letters in September 2025 to businesses not honoring GPC opt-out signals.
first_seen_or_mainstream: Signal specification existed since ~2021, but state-law mandates and enforcement activity making it a must-know marketer term concentrated in 2025-2026.

what_it_is: EU Digital Services Act (DSA) designation for online platforms with at least 45 million monthly active users in the EU, subject to the strictest transparency and advertising-disclosure obligations.
why_marketers_care: Marketers running campaigns on VLOPs (major social/search platforms) must meet DSA ad-transparency and targeting-disclosure rules; non-compliant companies risk fines up to 6% of global turnover (20% for repeat DMA gatekeeper violations).
example: DSA Article 46 codes of conduct for online advertising require platforms displaying ads and advertisers purchasing ads on VLOPs to participate in supply-chain transparency standards.
first_seen_or_mainstream: DSA VLOP obligations took effect August 2023, but marketer-facing ad-transparency codes of conduct and enforcement activity intensified through 2024-2025.

what_it_is: EU regulation setting mandatory rules for online platforms on content moderation, ad transparency, and targeted-advertising disclosure to keep users safe and markets fair.
why_marketers_care: Codes of conduct for online advertising (Article 46) require ad-supply-chain traceability; marketers targeting EU users must obey these rules or face fines, with several implementation deadlines landing in late 2025.
example: The DSA's advertising transparency requirements were discussed in an October 2025 EDPB public consultation response from ZAW (German advertising federation).
first_seen_or_mainstream: DSA entered force 2022-2023; ad-specific codes of conduct and marketer compliance activity concentrated 2024-2025.
notes: Legislation predates the window, but marketer-facing operational obligations and enforcement are newly mainstream in 2024-2025.

what_it_is: EU regulation that disciplines the economic power of designated 'gatekeeper' platforms (e.g. restricting self-preferencing and combining data across services without consent).
why_marketers_care: Gatekeeper obligations affect how marketers can target and measure on platforms like Google and Meta in the EU; repeat violations by gatekeepers can trigger fines up to 20% of global turnover, reshaping available targeting options.
example: Fasken's July 2025 overview explains how DMA gatekeeper rules interact with DSA advertising-transparency rules for EU-facing marketers.
first_seen_or_mainstream: DMA entered force 2022-2023; gatekeeper compliance changes affecting marketer workflows landed through 2024-2025.
notes: Legislation predates the window; included because gatekeeper-driven changes to targeting/consent options became operationally relevant to marketers in 2024-2025.

what_it_is: EU AI Act category for AI models capable of a wide range of tasks (training compute above 10^23 FLOP, generating language/image/video), now subject to transparency, copyright, and safety obligations under a dedicated Code of Practice.
why_marketers_care: Marketing teams using GPAI-based tools (copy generation, creative AI, chatbots) inherit compliance exposure; GPAI obligations began 2 August 2025, with full AI Office enforcement powers from 2 August 2026, directly affecting which AI marketing tools are usable in the EU.
example: The European Commission's General-Purpose AI Code of Practice (published 10 July 2025) organizes GPAI compliance into Transparency, Copyright, and Safety and Security chapters.
first_seen_or_mainstream: EU AI Act passed 2024; GPAI-specific obligations and Code of Practice took effect August 2025.

what_it_is: IAB Tech Lab standard that structures and transmits consumer data-deletion requests across the ad-tech supply chain, reducing manual handling of erasure requests between advertisers, platforms, and vendors.
why_marketers_care: Endorsed by the UK ICO in July 2025 and upgraded to V2 in October 2025 alongside GPP updates; gives marketers and their ad-tech partners a standardized, auditable way to honor deletion rights across complex programmatic supply chains.
example: IAB Tech Lab's Data Deletion Request Framework was formally recognized in the UK ICO's Online Tracking Strategy Update, per PR Newswire, July 2025.
first_seen_or_mainstream: Framework developed 2024-2025; ICO endorsement and V2 release in 2025 made it a live compliance topic.
notes: Still in public-comment/early-adoption stage as of late 2025; watch for broader uptake through 2026.

what_it_is: A standardized attention-measurement score (0-100), pioneered commercially by Adelaide, that synthesizes viewability, time-in-view, interaction, and contextual signals into one metric predicting ad efficacy; the IAB/MRC published joint Attention Measurement Guidelines in November 2025.
why_marketers_care: Google made AU a Custom Bidding signal in DV360 from mid-July 2026, and Amazon DSP launched Adelaide attention segments in June 2026 with a Quality Floor excluding MFA sites and low-AU placements — attention is moving from a research metric to an active bidding and buying lever.
example: Nielsen and Adelaide launched a unified reach-and-attention measurement view in 2025, per Nielsen's own newsroom release.
first_seen_or_mainstream: Adelaide's AU metric existed earlier, but IAB/MRC standardization (Nov 2025) and platform-level bidding integration (DV360, Amazon DSP) in 2026 made it newly mainstream.

what_it_is: Smart-TV technology that identifies exactly what content a viewer is watching (linear or streaming), generating viewing data used for CTV/TV ad targeting and measurement.
why_marketers_care: ACR data lets marketers de-duplicate CTV and linear TV exposure and target based on real viewing behavior, becoming a core input for 2025-2026 CTV measurement stacks as linear/streaming convergence accelerates.
example: Viant's advertiser guide explains how TV ACR data is used for cross-screen targeting and de-duplication.
first_seen_or_mainstream: ACR technology is not new (used since ~2015), but its role as a core, marketer-facing CTV measurement building block intensified through 2024-2026 as CTV ad spend grew.
notes: Technology predates the window; flagged because its marketer-facing prominence in CTV buying/measurement stacks is a 2024-2026 development.

what_it_is: Turkey's national database system (iys.org.tr) where businesses store and manage consumer consents for commercial electronic messages (SMS, email, calls); separate from and complementary to KVKK data-processing consent.
why_marketers_care: Turkish marketers must obtain İYS approval before sending commercial messages, on top of KVKK consent for processing personal data; since 31 March 2025 approval/rejection operations can only be performed through Official İYS Integrators, tightening compliance requirements for CRM and lifecycle marketing teams.
example: DSR Belgelendirme's 2026 guide documents current İYS application steps via MERSİS number and e-signature.
first_seen_or_mainstream: İYS system established under Turkey's e-commerce law (~2015-2020), but Integrator-only rule change (March 2025) and stricter 2026 penalty guidance made it newly urgent for marketers.
notes: System itself predates the window; included because operational rule changes (Integrator-only approvals, 2026 penalties) are newly relevant to Turkish marketers in this period.

what_it_is: A Google Ads Search-campaign feature (toggle) launched in 2025, bundling broad-match/keywordless query matching, AI-generated headline/description customization, and Final URL Expansion (FUE).
why_marketers_care: Rolling out fully by Q3 2025 and expanding into Dynamic Search Ads upgrades in 2026, AI Max delivers roughly 14% more conversions at similar CPA per Google's own data, making it a term PPC marketers must now know when planning Search budgets.
example: Google's own blog post 'Unlock next-level performance with AI Max for Search campaigns' documents the feature's rollout.
first_seen_or_mainstream: Announced/rolled out 2025 (previously private beta as 'Search Max'); expanded through 2026.
notes: Not a classic acronym (it's a product name), included as a short acronym-style term per task scope.

what_it_is: Low-quality websites engineered primarily to generate ad impressions via paid/clickbait traffic rather than to serve genuine editorial or utility value; no single industry-agreed definition exists.
why_marketers_care: Major buyers (e.g. GroupM) began excluding MFA sites from programmatic buys, and attention-scoring vendors (Adelaide) now build MFA-exclusion 'Quality Floors' directly into DSP segments (2026), making MFA avoidance a standard line item in media plans.
example: Digiday's oral history 'MFA should stand for made-for-arbitrage' traces the industry debate over the term's definition.
first_seen_or_mainstream: Term and industry crusade against MFA intensified from 2023 (GroupM ban) through 2024-2026 as ongoing definitional debates and buy-side exclusion lists matured.
notes: Origin of the term predates Sept 2024, but industry-wide operationalization (exclusion lists, quality floors) is concentrated in 2024-2026; borderline inclusion.

what_it_is: A browser-based, cookieless ad-attribution proposal (originally from Meta and Mozilla, now a W3C Private Advertising Technology Working Group draft) using differential privacy and secure aggregation to measure ad effectiveness without tracking individuals.
why_marketers_care: Represents one of several competing post-cookie measurement standards (alongside Google's Attribution Reporting API and Apple's Private Ads Measurement); the W3C's First Public Working Draft appeared in late 2025, signaling where cross-browser privacy-safe attribution standards may converge.
example: Mozilla's blog 'Privacy Preserving Attribution for Advertising' documents the original Meta/Mozilla proposal and its evolution into a W3C standard.
first_seen_or_mainstream: Proposed August 2024 (Mozilla/Meta); W3C draft progressed through 2025.
notes: Experimental; a Firefox implementation was tested and later removed, so real-world adoption is very low despite standards-track progress.

what_it_is: One of Google's Privacy Sandbox APIs (alongside Topics and Protected Audience) designed to measure ad conversions without cross-site tracking, using noised, aggregated reports instead of individual-level data.
why_marketers_care: Google announced on 17 October 2025 that it is retiring ARA along with nine other Privacy Sandbox technologies, citing low adoption; deprecation starts in Chrome 144 (Jan 2026) with full removal targeted for Chrome 150 (July 2026) — a major reversal marketers need to know when planning post-cookie measurement.
example: PerfxAd reported Google delayed then ultimately moved to retire the Attribution Reporting API rollout in 2025-2026.
first_seen_or_mainstream: API developed 2022-2024; became a live marketer topic through 2025 rollout attempts, then its October 2025 retirement announcement made it newly significant.
notes: Now being deprecated (not adopted), but the retirement itself is a significant, newly mainstream 2025-2026 story marketers must understand.

what_it_is: A Privacy Sandbox API intended for cookieless remarketing/retargeting, running on-device auctions instead of relying on third-party cookie-based audience lists.
why_marketers_care: Like ARA, Google announced its retirement on 17 October 2025 as part of a broader wind-down of ten Privacy Sandbox technologies, citing low adoption, with deprecation in Chrome starting January 2026 and full removal targeted July 2026, ending several years of marketer preparation for this alternative.
example: Google's October 2025 announcement retiring Privacy Sandbox technologies, covered by Segwise, lists Protected Audience among the retired APIs.
first_seen_or_mainstream: Developed 2022-2024, tested through 2025; retirement announced October 2025.
notes: Same retirement context as ARA; both are worth documenting precisely because marketers spent 2024-2025 preparing for APIs that are now being wound down.
